description: Propositional and predicate logic, proof, automated reasoning and the formal methods that use them to show programs and systems correct. Students build truth-table and proof tools, write SAT encodings, prove loops correct with invariants and model-check small concurrent systems.
modelledOn: Huth and Ryan, Logic in Computer Science
Baier and Katoen, Principles of Model Checking
Jackson, Software Abstractions: Logic, Language, and Analysis
outcomes: Translate specifications into propositional and first-order logic and decide validity, satisfiability and entailment.
Construct natural-deduction proofs and explain soundness and completeness of a proof system.
Encode combinatorial problems for a SAT solver and explain how DPLL and conflict-driven clause learning search.
Prove small programs correct using Hoare triples, weakest preconditions, loop invariants and variants.
Specify a concurrent system as a transition system, state properties in LTL and CTL, and check them by model checking.
Write and refine a formal specification of a small system and judge where formal methods are worth their cost.

units.title: Propositional logic
topics: Syntax and semantics; truth tables, tautologies, contradictions and satisfiability
Logical equivalence and entailment; the standard laws and substitution
Normal forms: negation, conjunctive and disjunctive; conversion algorithms
Structure-preserving transformation to linear-size CNF with fresh variables
Modelling with propositional logic: access policies, product configurations, circuit constraints

units.title: Predicate logic
topics: Syntax: terms, predicates, quantifiers, free and bound variables, substitution
Semantics: structures, interpretations, models and validity
Translating English specifications into first-order formulas; common quantifier mistakes
Equivalences, prenex normal form and Skolemisation
Equality, theories and the undecidability of first-order validity
Finite model finding and counter-model search for specifications

units.title: Natural deduction and proof
topics: Natural deduction rules for propositional logic: introduction and elimination, assumptions and discharge
Natural deduction rules for quantifiers and equality
Soundness and completeness of natural deduction; semantic versus syntactic consequence
Semantic tableaux and sequent calculus as proof search
Mechanised proof: tactics, structural induction and a first look at a proof assistant

units.title: SAT solving and decision procedures
topics: Resolution and refutation completeness
The DPLL algorithm: unit propagation, pure literals and backtracking
Conflict-driven clause learning: implication graphs, learned clauses, watched literals and restarts
Encoding problems as SAT: graph colouring, timetabling, Sudoku and pigeonhole
Satisfiability modulo theories: equality with uninterpreted functions, congruence closure, linear arithmetic
SAT and SMT in practice: configuration checking, bounded verification and test generation

units.title: Hoare logic and program correctness
topics: Programs as state transformers; assertions, preconditions and postconditions
Hoare triples and the rules for assignment, sequence, conditional and while
Weakest preconditions and strongest postconditions; the wp calculus
Partial versus total correctness; soundness of Hoare logic
Verification conditions and mechanised checking of annotated programs
Arrays, aliasing and a first look at separation logic

units.title: Loop invariants and termination
topics: Finding invariants: generalising postconditions, replacing constants by variables
Worked invariants: integer division, GCD, linear search, binary search, insertion sort
Termination: variants and well-founded orderings
Strengthening invariants and common invariant mistakes
Design by contract: pre- and postconditions, class invariants and runtime assertion checking

units.title: Temporal logic and model checking
topics: Transition systems and Kripke structures; modelling concurrent systems and interleaving
Safety, liveness and fairness properties
Linear temporal logic: syntax, semantics and typical specification patterns
Computation tree logic and CTL*; comparing LTL and CTL expressiveness
Explicit-state model checking: CTL labelling by fixpoint iteration, and Buchi automata for LTL
Symbolic model checking with BDDs and bounded model checking with SAT
State-space explosion, partial-order reduction, abstraction and counterexample interpretation

units.title: Specification languages and refinement
topics: Model-based specification: state, invariants and operations with pre- and postconditions
Relational specification and bounded analysis with an Alloy-style tool
Specifying concurrent and distributed protocols in a TLA+-style language
Refinement: data refinement, simulation relations and stepwise development
Formal methods in industry: railways, avionics, smart cards and mobile-money transaction logic
Cost, benefit and limits of formal methods; lightweight formal methods in everyday practice

schedule.title: Propositional logic: syntax, semantics, equivalence
schedule.exercise: Build the truth table for a three-variable formula, prove two equivalences with algebraic laws, and convert a formula to CNF and DNF by hand.

tasks.title: Generate truth tables for four given formulas in the logic tool and classify each as a tautology, contradiction or contingent formula
Test whether five pairs of formulas are equivalent and whether a given set of premises entails a conclusion, using truth tables
Write a program that converts any formula to negation normal form and CNF, and check it against truth tables on 20 random formulas

schedule.title: Linear-size CNF encoding and modelling
schedule.exercise: Encode an access policy for a clinic records system as a propositional formula, and apply the fresh-variable CNF transformation to a formula with five operators.

tasks.title: Apply the fresh-variable CNF transformation to a nested formula, list the clauses, and verify that the result is equisatisfiable with the original
Model a product configuration with six options and four constraints as propositional logic, then list all valid configurations by satisfying assignments
Write a checker for a role-based access policy as a formula, and find a user who is allowed to approve and pay the same invoice

schedule.title: First-order syntax, semantics and translation
schedule.exercise: Translate eight English sentences about students and courses into first-order logic, then give a structure that satisfies one formula and falsifies another.

tasks.title: Mark free and bound variables in six formulas and compute the result of substituting a term for a variable, avoiding capture
Evaluate quantified formulas over a small finite structure of 4 elements with two relations, and report the truth value of each
Review a draft contract-style specification for a mobile money transfer with quantifiers, find the ambiguity in two clauses, and rewrite them precisely

schedule.title: Normal forms, equality and decidability
schedule.exercise: Convert a formula to prenex form and Skolemise it, and explain in a paragraph why no program can decide validity of every first-order sentence.

tasks.title: Convert three formulas to prenex normal form, then Skolemise each and state which variables the Skolem functions depend on
Search all structures of size up to 4 for a model of a given set of axioms with a script, and report a counter-model for a false claim
Step through a rewriting system that decides equality in a small theory, and show a case where the process fails to terminate

schedule.title: Natural deduction and proof
schedule.exercise: Prove five sequents in natural deduction, one with quantifiers, and prove by structural induction that reversing a list twice returns the original list.

tasks.title: Build natural-deduction proofs for three propositional sequents in the proof checker, with every assumption discharged and every rule step accepted
Prove a quantified sequent such as 'for all x, P(x) and Q(x)' implies 'for all x, P(x)' using the quantifier rules correctly
Run a semantic tableau on a formula, close or leave open each branch, and read a counter-model from an open branch

schedule.title: Resolution and DPLL
schedule.exercise: Refute a small clause set by resolution, then run DPLL by hand on a ten-clause formula, showing each unit propagation and each backtrack.

tasks.title: Derive the empty clause from an unsatisfiable set of six clauses by resolution, drawing the proof tree and listing each resolvent
Trace DPLL on a 12-clause formula in the visualiser, noting each decision, unit propagation and backtrack until the formula is solved
Implement DPLL with unit propagation, then add clause learning on conflict, and compare decision counts on 10 benchmark formulas

schedule.title: Encoding problems and SMT
schedule.exercise: Encode a four-colouring of a map of Ghana's regions as SAT, write the constraints for a 4 by 4 Sudoku, and decide a small formula with equality and a function symbol.

tasks.title: Encode graph colouring of a ten-node map as CNF, solve it with the bundled solver, and decode the model into a valid colouring
Encode a weekly exam timetable with room, invigilator and clash constraints as SAT, and prove one extra constraint makes it unsatisfiable
Use congruence closure to decide whether a given set of equalities and disequalities over f and g terms is satisfiable

schedule.title: Hoare logic and weakest preconditions
schedule.exercise: Prove three small programs correct with Hoare rules, compute the weakest precondition of a conditional and a loop-free fragment, and distinguish partial from total correctness.

tasks.title: Prove a Hoare triple for a swap of two variables by applying the assignment and sequence rules step by step
Compute weakest preconditions backward through a program with assignments and a conditional, and simplify the resulting formula
Generate verification conditions for an annotated absolute-value and maximum program and check them with a theorem prover or solver

schedule.title: Loop invariants and termination
schedule.exercise: Find the invariant and variant for integer division by repeated subtraction and for binary search, and prove each loop correct and terminating.

tasks.title: Write down an invariant for a GCD loop, prove it holds initially and is preserved, and show it gives the postcondition on exit
Step through insertion sort in the visualiser and state the loop invariant on the sorted prefix after every outer iteration
Annotate a binary search with an invariant and variant, check it with runtime assertions on 1000 random arrays, and find the bug in a faulty version

schedule.title: Transition systems and temporal logic
schedule.exercise: Model two processes sharing a flag as a transition system, then write LTL and CTL formulas for mutual exclusion, absence of starvation and reachability.

tasks.title: Draw the state graph of two interleaved processes with a shared variable and count the reachable states and transitions
Classify given properties as safety or liveness and find a counterexample trace in a faulty traffic-light model
Write LTL formulas for six English requirements about a lift controller and check them on a given set of infinite traces

schedule.title: Model checking algorithms
schedule.exercise: Label the states of a small Kripke structure for EG, AU and EU by fixpoint iteration, and explain how bounded model checking uses a SAT solver.

tasks.title: Run the CTL labelling algorithm on a 10-state structure, showing the set of states satisfying each subformula at each iteration
Check the classic two-process flag-and-turn mutual exclusion algorithm for safety and liveness in the model checker, and read the counterexample for a broken variant
Implement explicit-state reachability with a hash set for a token-ring model, measure how states grow with the number of processes, and report the explosion

schedule.title: Model-based and relational specification
schedule.exercise: Specify a bank-account or mobile-money wallet system with state, an invariant and three operations, and use bounded analysis to find an invariant-breaking sequence.

tasks.title: Write a set-based specification of a library loan system with invariant and operations, and check that each operation preserves the invariant on examples
Specify a small file system as relations, assert that no directory is its own ancestor, and examine the counterexamples the bounded analysis finds
Model a two-phase commit protocol as a state machine, check that no node commits while another aborts, and examine a counterexample with a lost message

schedule.title: Refinement, industry practice and project
schedule.exercise: Refine an abstract set-based specification of a queue into an array-based design, argue why the refinement holds, and present your formal-methods project and a cost-benefit view.

tasks.title: Define an abstraction function from a concrete ring-buffer queue to an abstract sequence, and verify the simulation conditions for each operation
Judge in a case file whether formal methods are worth it for a mobile-money ledger, a ward stock tracker and a rail signalling controller, and defend the choices
Write property-based tests and assertions for an executable specification, and compare what they catch against what a model checker catches on the same model
